name: Adobe Firefly
pros: Licensed training data and commercial indemnity
files: Text prompts and image inputs, with deep integration into Adobe file formats.
value: Trained on licensed and public-domain material rather than an undisclosed web scrape, and sold with enterprise indemnity. For organizations where legal review gates creative tooling, that provenance position matters more than output quality.
engine: Adobe's own Firefly models, positioned on licensed training data.
latency: Fast enough for interactive editing inside the Creative Cloud applications.
quality: Good, and improving, though generally behind Midjourney on pure aesthetics. Its advantage is integration and legal posture rather than raw output.
tagline: Image generation built for commercial use, with indemnity, which is the point.
use_cases: Commercial marketing imagery where provenance must survive legal review
Generative editing inside Photoshop and Illustrator workflows already in place
Brand-controlled generation using an organization's own approved assets
integrations: Photoshop, Illustrator, Express, and the wider Creative Cloud
governance_note: This is the reference case for training-data provenance as a procurement criterion. Where a generator cannot say what it was trained on, the organization inherits that uncertainty on every asset it publishes. Firefly's commercial indemnity converts that uncertainty into a contractual allocation, which is exactly the sort of control an auditor can test. Content Credentials support also helps with the provenance-labelling obligations now appearing in AI law.
training_optout: Enterprise agreements cover customer content use. Adobe's position on training data provenance is the product's central claim and should be read directly rather than taken second-hand.
